top.description: Nigeria’s historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup has brought head coach Akeem Ishola Busari into the spotlight after he guided the Flamingos to their first-ever title in the competition. The Nigerian girls defeated Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, 2026, in Morocco, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Busari’s achievement is particularly remarkable because he was appointed head coach only seven months before the tournament, having inherited a team that had previously finished third at the 2022 edition. Here are five things to know about the coach behind Nigeria’s historic achievement. 1. He is a CAF A-licensed coach Akeem Busari arrives in the role with a long coaching career behind him. A CAF A-licensed coach, he has worked across both men’s and women’s football in Nigeria and abroad, building a reputation for discipline and attacking football. His coaching experience spans more than three decades, with stints at several Nigerian clubs, including Shooting Stars, Gateway United, JSP FC and Bayelsa Queens. He has also worked in the Republic of Benin. 2. He received his coaching training at the National Institute for Sports The Flamingos coach began his formal coaching education at the National Institute for Sports (NIS), Lagos, where he obtained his initial coaching qualification in 1999. According to NIS Director-General Philip Shaibu, Busari subsequently returned to complete the institute’s higher programmes between 2003 and 2006. He received his final coaching certificates in October 2006. His training at the institute preceded his appointment to the national team by nearly two decades. 3. He previously coached several Nigerian clubs Before taking charge of the Flamingos, Busari built his coaching career across several Nigerian clubs. He was head coach of Pacesetter Queens FC in Ibadan before his appointment to the national team. His previous experience also includes working with Shooting Stars, Gateway United, JSP FC and Bayelsa Queens. He played a role in helping Shooting Stars secure promotion to the top flight during the 2008/2009 season. He also won multiple State FA Cup titles with Gateway United and Shooting Stars. In 2023, he guided JSP FC to promotion in the Benin Championship League. He also served as Technical Director of Bayelsa Queens, one of Nigeria’s established women’s football clubs. 4. He was appointed Flamingos coach in April 2026 The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) announced Busari’s appointment as head coach of the Flamingos on April 2, 2026. He replaced Bankole Olowookere, who had guided Nigeria to a bronze medal at the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in India. At the time of his appointment, Busari was the head coach of Pacesetter Queens. His immediate responsibility was to lead Nigeria through the qualifying campaign for the 2026 tournament in Morocco. top.title: Fran Gonzalez explains his decision to leave Real Madrid – “You have other dreams”
top.description: Fran Gonzalez explains his decision to leave Real Madrid – “You have other dreams” Fran Gonzalez was one of the less talked-about exits for Real Madrid in a summer that was saw a lot of action. The young goalkeeper, after multiple years with the club’s academy, left Real Madrid to join Sevilla on a deal worth €3 million . Although Gonzalez has yet to make a breakthrough at Sevilla, he has recently explained his decision to leave Real Madrid in the summer in great detail. Gonzalez on leaving Real Madrid Fran Gonzalez only ever featured in one game for Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) When asked about his decision to leave the Spanish capital, Gonzalez pointed some key reasons including the desire to make it elsewhere. “I had closed a chapter there in Madrid, with Castilla, and I believed the best thing for me was to take that leap, wherever it might be,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). “Obviously, it’s normal for young goalkeepers not to play right away, no matter where they go, because I come from the Primera RFEF, a competition that has improved a lot in recent years, but it’s a big step. I feel very prepared to make that leap,” he added. Gonzalez explained he had felt his time at Real Madrid academy had come to an end and it was time for a new challenge elsewhere. “I felt that I had finished a stage, and Sevilla is one of the great clubs in Spain, a truly historic club, very good in every sense, and a real opportunity for me to compete and play in the coming years, ” he said. Gonzalez on joining Sevilla Fran Gonzalez spent multiple years at La Fabrica . (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Gonzalez admitted it was quite painful to leave Valdebebas, as he hailed Real Madrid as the best club in the world. However, the goalkeeper admitted it was his desire to join Sevilla and that he was drawn to the opportunity. “It’s not easy to leave what is probably the best club in the world, but well, many times you have other dreams and my dream was to come to Sevilla, from the first moment I was very clear about it. “I didn’t even have to think about it, it’s a place to continue growing and to be able to stay for a long time ,” he concluded. Gonzalez’s spell at Sevilla, though, has started off slowly, with his only appearance this season coming in Copa Del Rey. He is still comfortably behind Odysseas Vlachodimos in the pecking order. However, the young Spaniard is confident he can soon fight for a place in the first-team and is ready to exercise patience.

top.description: Former NFL reporter Dianna Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Returning to NFL reporting after a public controversy is difficult enough, but rebuilding trust with fellow insiders may be an even bigger challenge for Dianna Russini. Her rumored plans to return to sports media have already drawn a firm response from Pro Football Talk founder Mike Florio, who says he will not pass along her future reports without independent confirmation, leaving Russini with a serious question to address before making her comeback. Mike Florio Challenges Dianna Russini to Restore Her Credibility Florio explained his position during an appearance on “PFT Live,” where he questioned whether Russini could regain the credibility needed to work as an NFL insider. He said his role involves sharing and validating reports from other journalists, but he cannot do that when he does not trust the original source. “If there’s going to be actual reporting as part of this, you’ve gotta have some credibility, or nobody’s going to believe what you say,” Florio said . “Is there going to be an effort to be an insider again?” He made it clear that Russini’s previous explanations have not changed his position. Florio said he would not amplify her work unless another reporter without similar credibility concerns independently confirmed the information. “After everything that’s happened, everything we know, I’m not going to be inclined to believe anything. Which means I’m not going to be amplifying anything,” Florio said. “I don’t care what the reporting is. Unless and until it’s confirmed by someone who doesn’t have these credibility issues, I’m going to ignore it. Unless the credibility is somehow restored.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The dispute traces back to April, when Page Six published photographs of Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel together at a resort in Sedona, Arizona. Russini and The Athletic initially described the meeting as a coincidental gathering involving a larger group. However, reports later surfaced about previous encounters, including a boat outing in Tennessee in 2021. Russini resigned from The Athletic on April 14 while denying a romantic relationship with Vrabel. A subsequent five-month internal review examined more than 900 stories, videos, and podcasts. (William Purnell-Imagn Images) The SEC has explained why replays let the fumble call on Arch Manning’s third-quarter throw stand. The ruling kept alive the drive that started No. 7 Texas on a run of 21 straight points in a 34-20 win at No. 18 Missouri. Manning was hit on his arm as he tried to throw on third-and-10. Officials ruled it a fumble that Texas recovered for a first down, and the call stood after review. However, the league’s explanation didn’t satisfy a number of critics, one of whom pointed to an official’s signal on the play, while Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz chose not to blame the officials to avoid paying a hefty fine. How the Arch Manning Fumble Unfolded and What the Rulebook Says Texas trailed 20-13 and faced third-and-10 at the Missouri 39 with 2:22 left in the third quarter when Tigers linebacker Brian Huff caught Manning’s right arm as he tried to throw. The ball came loose, sailed forward and landed downfield, where no Missouri defender got to it. Texas receiver Emmett Mosley V scooped it up at the Missouri 25, four yards past the line to gain, and officials ruled it a fumble recovered by Texas. The ruling held up on replay, which spared Texas a fourth-and-10 at the Missouri 39 and served the Longhorns a fresh set of downs on a silver platter. Three plays later, Manning hit Jermaine Bishop Jr. for a 25-yard touchdown to tie the game at 20, and the Longhorns took their first lead of the day on his 23-yard scoring pass to Raleek Brown with 5:03 to play. The SEC laid out its reasoning in a statement after the game. “The ruling on the field was a fumble. nigeria.title: 5 things to know about Nigeria’s U-17 World Cup-winning coach, Akeem Busari
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup has brought head coach Akeem Ishola Busari into the spotlight after he guided the Flamingos to their first-ever title in the competition. The Nigerian girls defeated Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, 2026, in Morocco, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Busari’s achievement is particularly remarkable because he was appointed head coach only seven months before the tournament, having inherited a team that had previously finished third at the 2022 edition. Here are five things to know about the coach behind Nigeria’s historic achievement. 1. He is a CAF A-licensed coach Akeem Busari arrives in the role with a long coaching career behind him. A CAF A-licensed coach, he has worked across both men’s and women’s football in Nigeria and abroad, building a reputation for discipline and attacking football. His coaching experience spans more than three decades, with stints at several Nigerian clubs, including Shooting Stars, Gateway United, JSP FC and Bayelsa Queens. He has also worked in the Republic of Benin. 2. He received his coaching training at the National Institute for Sports The Flamingos coach began his formal coaching education at the National Institute for Sports (NIS), Lagos, where he obtained his initial coaching qualification in 1999. According to NIS Director-General Philip Shaibu, Busari subsequently returned to complete the institute’s higher programmes between 2003 and 2006. He received his final coaching certificates in October 2006. His training at the institute preceded his appointment to the national team by nearly two decades. 3. He previously coached several Nigerian clubs Before taking charge of the Flamingos, Busari built his coaching career across several Nigerian clubs. He was head coach of Pacesetter Queens FC in Ibadan before his appointment to the national team. His previous experience also includes working with Shooting Stars, Gateway United, JSP FC and Bayelsa Queens. He played a role in helping Shooting Stars secure promotion to the top flight during the 2008/2009 season. He also won multiple State FA Cup titles with Gateway United and Shooting Stars. In 2023, he guided JSP FC to promotion in the Benin Championship League. He also served as Technical Director of Bayelsa Queens, one of Nigeria’s established women’s football clubs. 4. He was appointed Flamingos coach in April 2026 The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) announced Busari’s appointment as head coach of the Flamingos on April 2, 2026. He replaced Bankole Olowookere, who had guided Nigeria to a bronze medal at the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in India. At the time of his appointment, Busari was the head coach of Pacesetter Queens. His immediate responsibility was to lead Nigeria through the qualifying campaign for the 2026 tournament in Morocco. He subsequently guided the team past Benin Republic with an 8-5 aggregate victory to secure their World Cup

nigeria.title: Troops rescue 119 civilians, recover eight vehicles in Borno
nigeria.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have rescued 119 civilians abducted by terrorists and recovered eight vehicles during an operation in Borno. The military disclosed this in an operational report made available to Newsmen on Saturday in Abuja. The report said the operation was conducted by troops of 135 Special Forces Battalion while monitoring surveillance cameras along the Dutsen Kura-Bulazarma-Kamuya road. It said the troops sighted the terrorists abducting civilians and vehicles and mobilised through Mangari-Dora in Biu Local Government Area to foil the operation. According to the report, they engaged the terrorists, forcing them to abandon the abducted civilians and flee in disarray. It said the troops recovered eight vehicles and reunited the rescued civilians with their families. “They also discovered and detonated an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) around the Bam-Buratai Junction-Bulazarma general area. “In a separate development, a suspected fighter of Jama’atu Ahlis-Sunna Lidda’Awati Wal-Jihad (JAS) surrendered to troops of 202 Battalion at Ngurusoye Village, Bama Local Government Area. “The suspect reportedly fled his group’s enclave in Bula Daloye following clashes with the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and hardship. “He surrendered with an FN rifle and seven rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and is currently in military custody for further action,” it said. The report said troops and members of the Hybrid Force arrested a suspected terrorist informant and collaborator at Ngamdu Town, Borno, on Nov. 5. It added that troops of Army Headquarters Garrison foiled an attempted abduction of a retired senior military officer and his son at Kurudu Phase Five, Abuja. According to the report, the assailants attacked the residence of the retired officer at about 4:05 a.m. on Saturday, adding that troops’ intervention forced the attackers to abandon their victims after inflicting knife wounds on their shoulders and heads. The report added that the injured victims were evacuated to a nearby hospital for medical attention. It said the troops of Operation Enduring Peace arrested two suspected burglars at Doi Community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau on Saturday. The report said the suspects were allegedly attempting to break into a poultry house to steal chickens and were handed over to the police for further investigation. “In Benue, troops of Operation Whirl Stroke arrested a herder over alleged malicious grazing on farmland at Tse Tur, Gwer West Local Government Area. “The suspect was arrested at Umbago and remains in military custody for further action,” it said The post Troops rescue 119 civilians, recover eight vehicles in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Inuwa seeks common Northern policy framework to tackle out-of-school children
nigeria.description: Advocates unified regional agenda, investment in agriculture, agro-allied industries to combat poverty, insecurity Sultan applauds Gombe governor’s Almajiri education reforms By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Gombe State Governor and Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has called for a common policy framework and unified regional agenda to sustain education reforms, tackle the growing number of out-of-school children and accelerate human capital development across Northern Nigeria. The governor said addressing the region’s educational challenges required a coordinated approach that went beyond school enrolment to include poverty reduction, improved security, economic empowerment and the creation of sustainable livelihood opportunities for the growing population. Yahaya made the call at the 2026 Biennial Lecture and Awards Ceremony of the Barewa Old Boys Association (BOBA), held in Gombe, with the theme, “The Scourge of Out-of-School Children and the Implications for National Security.” Describing the theme as timely and critical to the future of Northern Nigeria, the governor warned that the increasing number of children outside the formal education system posed serious threats to social stability, economic productivity and national security. He observed that educational exclusion perpetuated poverty, widened inequality and exposed vulnerable children and young people to criminal exploitation, radicalisation and other antisocial tendencies. Yahaya recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2019, Gombe State had more than 500,000 out-of-school children, explaining that sustained interventions by his government had brought approximately 350,000 of them back into the classroom. He attributed the achievement to the declaration of a state of emergency in the education sector, construction of mega schools with expanded learning capacities, recruitment of more than 1,000 qualified teachers and establishment of Almajiri Integrated Learning Centres, among other initiatives. Drawing from the state’s experience, the governor urged Northern states to move away from fragmented interventions and embrace a common regional framework that would identify successful educational models, encourage their adoption across state boundaries and guarantee continuity. He proposed that the Northern States Governors’ Forum should provide the institutional platform for harmonising educational policies, coordinating priorities and strengthening collaboration among the 19 Northern states. According to him, a unified Northern Agenda would ensure that successful programmes initiated by successive administrations were sustained, while promoting the sharing of resources, expertise and best practices for regional development. He maintained that the magnitude of the challenges confronting Northern Nigeria required collective responsibility, stressing that no single state could effectively address the problem of out-of-school children in isolation

nigeria.title: Ebonyi govt lifts suspension on Ambertone as Ishiagu Community buries slain youths
nigeria.description: By Chiamaka Ekwuwe The Ebonyi State Government has lifted the temporary suspension on mining operations at the Ambertone Logistics Limited facility, operated by Zotmann Mining Limited, in Ihetutu community, Ishiagu, Ivo Local Government Area, following consultations with relevant stakeholders and the burial of two youths who died in a shooting incident in the area. The resumption of operations on Wednesday followed days of engagements involving the state government, representatives of the mining company, bereaved families and community stakeholders aimed at restoring peace and normalcy. The development comes after the deaths of Chibuike Elema, 18, and Obinna Gideon Akandu, 20, in a shooting incident reportedly involving a military officer on Sunday, October 18, 2026. The precise circumstances surrounding the incident, including the events leading to the shooting and the responsibility of the personnel involved, remain subject to clarification by the appropriate authorities. Available accounts indicate that the incident occurred approximately three kilometres from the company’s operational facility, reportedly near another mining concession. Following the incident, tensions reportedly escalated in the community, with some youths allegedly attacking the mining company’s facility, resulting in damage to vehicles, equipment, offices and other property. In response to the developments and concerns over public safety, the Ebonyi State Government ordered a temporary suspension of mining activities at the affected facility to prevent further escalation and facilitate peace-building efforts. Following consultations and reconciliation engagements, the government subsequently announced the lifting of the suspension, allowing operations to resume. Ambertone, Zotmann Clarify Company Identity The incident also generated conflicting reports concerning the identity of the mining company operating the affected facility. While some initial reports associated the incident with Palladium Mining Company, subsequent clarification from company representatives identified Ambertone Logistics Limited as the company whose facility was affected by the unrest. Representatives further clarified that Palladium Mining Company operates a separate facility in the community and is distinct from Ambertone Logistics Limited and its operational partner, Zotmann Mining Limited. The clarification was issued to address confusion arising from reports that appeared to have linked Palladium Mining Company to the incident. Representatives of Ambertone and Zotmann also stated that neither company authorised the shooting, maintaining that the incident occurred outside their operational premises. The circumstances surrounding the shooting and any possible responsibility of individuals involved remain separate matters requiring appropriate investigation. nigeria.title: Yoruba started home video, not Nollywood — Osuofia
nigeria.description: Veteran Nollywood actor, Nkem Owoh, popularly known as Osuofia, has clarified his position on the origins of Nigeria’s home-video industry, insisting that Yoruba filmmakers pioneered home-video productions but did not start Nollywood. Owoh made the clarification during an appearance on Curiosity Made Me Ask, hosted by comedian and content creator Adebayo Abidemi, popularly known as Bae U. The interview, published on the host’s YouTube channel on Saturday, featured the actor responding to a question about reports that he had claimed Yoruba people, rather than the Igbo, started Nollywood. The clarification comes amid an ongoing debate over the contributions of different ethnic groups to the development of Nigeria’s film industry. The debate gained fresh attention in August 2026 when late veteran actor Francis Duru argued that the Igbo built Nollywood but that Yoruba filmmakers had become more dominant because of their ability to organise and promote their productions. Duru, who died in October, had attributed much of the growth of the modern home-video industry in the 1990s and early 2000s to Igbo entrepreneurs. Reacting to the reported interpretation of his earlier comments, Owoh said it was inaccurate to suggest that he claimed Yoruba people started Nollywood, explaining that the name did not exist when filmmakers began producing movies. “First of all, you have given me this wrong accusation that I said, Yoruba started Nollywood. No. Yoruba started this film on… when did Nollywood come out? When we started the thing, there was no Nollywood as a name. “We sat together and we’re banding, you know, ideas and all that, how the thing is going to come to fruition. And eventually, we chose Nollywood,” he said. The actor, however, credited Yoruba filmmakers with popularising home-video productions in Nigeria, specifically mentioning veteran filmmaker Hubert Ogunde and Adebayo Papa as among those whose works he admired. “So, Yoruba started the thing. They made the thing very popular home video and all that. Yes, they did. And I’ve said it several. Okay. Ogunde and Adebayo Papa. These are the people I love to watch their thing,” he said. When the interviewer jokingly suggested that Ogunde was Igbo, Owoh disagreed, insisting that the late filmmaker was Yoruba. “Ogunde is not Igbo. I’m telling you that Yoruba started it. When Ogunde was out, I don’t think there was any Igbo man who was that popular in that,” he added. He further emphasised the distinction between the origins of home-video productions and Nollywood, stating: “The Yoruba did not start Nollywood. They started Home video.” Historical accounts of Nigerian cinema trace the development of Yoruba filmmaking to travelling theatre groups led by figures such as Hubert Ogunde and Duro Ladipo, whose stage productions evolved into film and video productions decades before the commercial home-video boom of the 1990s. nigeria.title: Messi wins second consecutive MLS Golden Boot after scoring 26 goals
nigeria.description: Inter Miami’s Lionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday after the defending champions took second place in the Eastern Conference with a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season. The Argentine superstar did not score but set up the first two goals at Miami’s Nu Stadium, both from corners, to help procure his club a home-field advantage for the first two playoff rounds. Messi’s 26 goals this season were enough to make him the first back-to-back MLS Golden Boot award winner. Petar Musa of Dallas was second on 22, not scoring in his club’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado. Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada’s brace soon after the break sparked a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko’s late strike. Runaway overall leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record for a season with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. At 23-3 with eight drawn, Nashville won the East and broke the mark of 74 points set by Miami in 2024. Miami finished second in the East on 60 points as third-place New England failed to take advantage of Inter’s draw with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando to end on 58. Messi’s men will face Columbus to begin the MLS playoffs. Other East matchups send New England against Philadelphia, Charlotte against Chicago and top seed Nashville against the wild-card winner, Orlando or Cincinnati. Columbus took advantage of the Cincinnati loss with a 4-3 victory at Chicago to finish seventh and avoid the wild card round. At Miami, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring. Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0. De Paul made it three before halftime, but Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors early and bagged a second in the 55th minute. In the 90th, Aloko bagged the equalizer, responding first to the ball as Smalls’s shot ricocheted off the post. A visibly frustrated Messi hit the post in stoppage time before Aloko came inches from bagging an unlikely winner with a thunderous shot into the outside netting. – Seattle, Real advance – Western Conference champion Vancouver beat Canadian rivals Montreal 2-0 to finish second overall, giving the Whitecaps a home-field edge if they should face Inter Miami in a rematch of last year’s MLS Cup final. There were six teams fighting for the last three Western Conference playoff spots on “Decision Day” with every MLS squad on the pitch. Portland, Colorado and the Los Angeles Galaxy needed only to win to secure a playoff berth but only Portland did so, the Timbers winning 2-0 at Austin while Real Salt Lake beat the Galaxy 2-1 and Colorado fell at Dallas, which allowed Real into the post-season. Seattle claimed the other spot with a 2-1 home win over Los Angeles FC. Albert Rusnak scored in the first minute

nigeria.title: Iran executes three men linked to anti-government protests
nigeria.description: Iranian authorities have executed three men convicted of carrying out operations on behalf of Israel and the United States during anti-government protests in January, the country’s judiciary has announced. The death sentences against Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were carried out on Sunday after being upheld by the Supreme Court, the judiciary’s Mizan Online website reported. According to the report, the three men were found guilty of “participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups” during the protests. Mizan said the defendants threw Molotov cocktails and grenades, used bladed weapons and firearms, and set fire to public facilities in Karaj, a city west of Tehran. Other defendants in the case received prison sentences ranging from five to 10 years, the report added. The protest movement, which initially erupted in December over the rising cost of living, rapidly developed into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on January 8 and 9. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths during the unrest, blaming the violence on what they described as “terrorist acts” orchestrated by the United States and Israel. However, foreign-based non-governmental organisations have reported higher casualty figures and maintained that Iranian security forces fired on protesters. The number of executions in Iran has increased since the outbreak of the Middle East war, which was triggered in late February by US and Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic. nigeria.title: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos forward, Oluebube Umejiaku, has explained how the team recovered from their opening defeat to Poland to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria began their campaign with a 2-1 loss to Poland, despite Umejiaku scoring as a substitute. However, the team bounced back, treating every subsequent fixture as a final on their way to winning the competition. The Flamingos defeated DPR Korea, Mexico and other opponents before overcoming Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to claim the trophy. Umejiaku, who started the tournament on the bench, became one of Nigeria’s standout performers, scoring crucial goals, including in the final, and winning the Golden Ball award as the tournament’s best player. Speaking to FIFA.com after Nigeria’s historic triumph, she said the players were determined to change their fortunes following the opening loss to Poland. “When we lost the first game against Poland, everybody said we needed to wake up because we didn’t come here to look at anybody’s face and we have to take every game as a final. We don’t downgrade anything; we play and we put all our best into every game.” Umejiaku also reflected on her journey from a substitute to one of the tournament’s most influential players, saying she remained hopeful of getting an opportunity to start. “Every time I went to training and every time I slept, I told God that I’m praying for all the people that are starting. But when I wanted to start, I just told God that it is my time,” she said. Another key contributor to Nigeria’s triumph was Awawu Bashiru, who initially had limited playing time under head coach Akeem Busari. Bashiru played just 77 minutes between the opening match and the quarter-final against Venezuela before earning her first start against Brazil. She scored twice in that encounter and also opened the scoring in the final against Japan. Reflecting on the team’s achievement, Bashiru credited their success to teamwork and the technical crew’s instructions. “I’m so happy, I’m so excited and I’m so grateful,” she said. “The teamwork, instruction and listening to our coaches is why we got the goals and why we won the final. We are history-makers. We made Nigeria, and the millions of people there, proud.” Busari, meanwhile, explained that his decisions to change the starting line-up were based on the players’ attitude, character and commitment rather than reputation. “No matter how good you are, I’m a coach that plays on character,” Busari said of making those key changes. “It’s all about mindset, attitude and merit; if they’re there, you get your playing time. If they’re not there, you’re waiting to come in. As a coach, we want everyone to wire up and play together.” Nigeria’s victory made the country the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first from the continent to claim a women’s FIFA tournament title. nigeria.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Eisenkot to form new government
nigeria.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an election that left both his camp and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition short of a parliamentary majority. Herzog’s office announced on Saturday night that the president had informed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, of his intention to give him the mandate to form a government. The formal appointment is expected to take place at a ceremony at the president’s residence in Jerusalem on Sunday. “This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X following the announcement. The decision brings Eisenkot closer to replacing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, after the religious-nationalist coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s camp secured 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc won 48, leaving both short of the 61 seats required to form a government. During consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received endorsements from two Arab-majority political lists, whose support could prove crucial in the coalition-building process. However, uncertainty remains over whether Eisenkot’s bloc would accept a formal alliance with the Arab-led parties, particularly after more than three years of war in Gaza. Netanyahu has opposed any arrangement involving the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government with what he described as “terrorist supporters”. He has also called for a national unity government. Eisenkot, however, has indicated a willingness to work with Arab-led parties under certain conditions, including their acceptance that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled. He has also pledged to take action against extremist Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank accused of attacking Palestinians, describing the incidents as “Jewish terror” allegedly enabled by Netanyahu’s government. Despite his willingness to engage with Arab-led parties, Eisenkot opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He has also vowed to end Hamas’ rule in Gaza and destroy its military wing. Eisenkot served as Israel’s Chief of General Staff from 2015 to 2019 and commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah. During the conflict, he developed the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”, a military strategy advocating the use of overwhelming force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by Hezbollah. Under the Israeli constitutional process, Eisenkot has 28 days to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers and form a government. Herzog can grant him an additional 14 days if he fails to meet the deadline. If Eisenkot cannot secure a parliamentary majority within the allotted period, the president may offer the mandate to another candidate. Failure by any candidate to form a government

nigeria.title: WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) has renewed its push for greater participation of women in business and leadership, identifying mentorship, visibility and empowerment as key tools for helping women access opportunities and advance their careers. The Executive Head of WIMBIZ, Omowunmi Akingbohungbe, said the organisation was committed to inspiring and empowering women to attain leadership positions while equipping them to become entrepreneurs. Speaking during an interview at the organisation’s 25th annual conference in Lagos, Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ connects experienced and accomplished women with emerging leaders to guide them through the challenges of building careers and businesses. “We’re big on mentoring. We connect mentors, accomplished and experienced women with rising leaders so they can handhold them and show them the path so they’re not reinventing the wheel,” she said. She also stressed the importance of visibility, noting that women needed to make their abilities known, develop confidence and put themselves forward for leadership opportunities. According to her, many women often hold back from applying for leadership positions because they feel they are not qualified, whereas men are more likely to take the chance. “Most times women will think I’m not qualified and all of that, but men would apply. And we also have the potential,” she said. Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ was therefore working to ensure women recognise their capabilities and have the confidence to pursue opportunities in business and public service. “At WIMBIZ, we train, mentor, empower women. We give women a right to be entrepreneurs at the same time,” she added. She described the organisation’s partnership with Autos, its official automobile partner for the annual conference, as part of its 25th anniversary celebrations. She said the partnership would also provide discounts to WIMBIZ members and free vehicle servicing for two years. The 25th annual conference was held under the theme, “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World.” The post WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: FIFA U-17 WWC: Why we lost to Nigeria in final – Japan coach Shirai
nigeria.description: Japan U-17 women’s national team coach, Sadayoshi Shirai, has praised Nigeria’s Flamingos following his side’s 2-1 defeat in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Shirai admitted that Nigeria’s speed and physical strength posed major problems for his players, particularly when the Flamingos managed to break through their defence. Nigeria secured the title through goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Awawu Bashiru, while Fuki Ito scored for Japan. Reacting after the encounter, Shirai acknowledged Nigeria’s superiority but maintained that his players gave their best throughout the final. “First of all, I have to say that Nigeria were a very strong team. We understood their strengths, but there were moments when they managed to get in behind our defence. Even so, I think our players fought incredibly hard until the very end, doing everything they could to cope with Nigeria’s speed and physical power. I also believe that if we had managed to score earlier, we might have had a better chance of winning the match. I want them [Japan’s players] to be proud of themselves. The way they fought until the very end of this World Cup will have inspired many people, and I hope they can take confidence from that,” Shirai said. Japan reached the final after defeating DPR Korea in the semi-finals, while Nigeria booked their place in the title decider with a victory over Brazil. The Flamingos eventually defeated Japan to claim the U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy, marking a historic achievement for Nigerian women’s football. nigeria.title: INEC to meet over Atiku’s 2027 ADC ticket
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will meet next week to consider the implications of the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), including the emergence of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The commission said it would not take a position on the party’s leadership crisis until it obtained and examined the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment. The Federal High Court in Abuja had, on Thursday, nullified the Mark-led caretaker committee and invalidated decisions taken under its leadership, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Sunday, INEC National Commissioner and Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, said the commission would not rely on media reports to determine the court’s position. “We can’t take a position until we see the judgment ourselves. We have to get the Certified True Copy because we don’t take decisions or reports of what the court said based on reports because the reports could be wrong,” he said. Haruna added that the commission would deliberate on the matter at its meeting next week. “Well, this one is very straightforward. Even then, we are all here till next week when the commission meets. We will have to meet over it,” he said. He also said INEC would comply with any further court order arising from an appeal by the Mark-led faction. “Obviously, if the David Mark faction should appeal, which I am sure they will, and they get an injunction for stay of execution, obviously, we’ll have to obey that judgment,” he added. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, had on Thursday nullified the leadership of the Mark-led caretaker committee, ruling that its emergence contravened the ADC constitution, relevant provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution. The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by a former ADC Deputy National Chairman (North-East), Nafiu Bala Gombe, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the caretaker committee assumed control of the party. Gombe argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was constitutionally entitled to take over its leadership. He consequently asked the court to invalidate the actions of the Mark-led leadership and restrain Mark and former Minister of Interior, Rauf Aregbesola, from parading themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary of the party, respectively. In its ruling, the court nullified the process through which the caretaker committee emerged and the party conducted its presidential primary that produced Atiku as its flag bearer for the 2027 elections. nigeria.title: U-17 WWC: Full list of award winners
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos emerged as the champions of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on Saturday in Morocco. The victory saw Nigeria secure the title , with Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scoring to seal the win for the Flamingos. DPR Korea’s Kim Son-gyong received the Golden Glove award for the best goalkeeper, while Japan was presented with the FIFA Fair Play Trophy. nigeria.title: Nigerians debate how much money is enough for Detty December
nigeria.description: Nigerians have taken to social media to debate how much money is enough to enjoy Detty December, with proposed budgets ranging from ₦50,000 to ₦15 million. The discussion began after financial services company Cowrywise asked Nigerians how much they considered a reasonable budget for the festive season in a post on X. The question generated different reactions, reflecting varying expectations and spending plans for the December festivities. While some users suggested modest amounts, others indicated that enjoying the season could require millions of naira. One X user, Ernest Onah, said ₦50,000 would be enough for him, prompting Cowrywise to question whether he planned to stay indoors throughout the festivities. How much money is a reasonable budget for Detty December? — Cowrywise (@cowrywise) November 4, 2026 Another user, Farouk Umar, proposed a budget of ₦1 million, while Philip Stanislaus suggested ₦500,000 and was asked to explain how he arrived at the figure. At the higher end, another respondent, identified as Great~MUHD, suggested ₦15 million as a reasonable amount for Detty December. However, some users appeared less interested in spending money on the festivities. One respondent, VictorBen, jokingly said he would rather spend ₦3 million buying a MacBook and sleeping throughout December. Detty December has become a popular expression for Nigeria’s end-of-year entertainment season, characterised by concerts, nightlife, parties, travel, social gatherings and other festive activities. The period, particularly in Lagos, attracts Nigerians in the diaspora and international visitors, while entertainment venues, hospitality businesses and event organisers often experience increased activity. However, the latest debate highlights the different financial expectations surrounding the season, as Nigerians weigh the cost of entertainment and social activities against their personal budgets. nigeria.title: Two waterway accidents kill police officer, woman in Bayelsa
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Two separate waterway accidents in Bayelsa State have claimed the lives of a serving police officer and a female passenger, the state Police Command has confirmed. The incidents occurred in Brass and Sagbama Local Government Areas, according to a statement issued on Saturday night by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed. The first accident involved a passenger boat that capsized along the Abedigbene waterways in Brass LGA on Thursday while travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa with eight persons on board, including a serving commissioner. The police said Maritime Union workers in Brass reported the incident, prompting a search-and-rescue operation by personnel of the Nigerian Navy’s Forward Operating Base (FOB) FORMOSO, in collaboration with local divers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community. Seven passengers were rescued, including the Bayelsa State Commissioner for Trade and Commerce, Dr Ebiere Jones, and an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. However, a serving police officer who was initially reported missing was subsequently confirmed dead. The second accident occurred at about 5:20 a.m. on Saturday, November 7, along the shoreline of Angalabiri Community in Sagbama LGA, when a tanker vessel belonging to Sterling Global Oil Ltd reportedly collided with canoes navigating close to the shoreline. According to the police, preliminary investigations indicated that the vessel struck and destroyed some of the canoes. One of the victims, identified as Mrs Victoria Abetnigo, an indigene of Angalabiri, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Ebedebiri General Hospital for treatment. She was, however, pronounced dead by the attending doctor. Her remains have been deposited at Ofoni Mortuary, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Reacting to the two tragedies, the Commissioner of Police, Bayelsa State Command, CP Ajao Saka Adewale, expressed sadness over the incidents and extended his condolences to the families, colleagues and loved ones of the deceased. The police commissioner particularly lamented the death of the serving police officer, praying for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased and strength for their families to bear the losses. He also commended the Nigerian Navy’s FOB FORMOSO, local divers, Maritime Union workers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community for their prompt intervention during the rescue operation. Adewale urged boat operators and commercial vessel owners to exercise caution and comply strictly with maritime safety regulations. He specifically called on vessel operators to maintain safe distances from shorelines and established canoe routes and avoid reckless navigation. He also advised passengers to wear life jackets throughout their journeys and urged all waterway users to prioritise safety and promptly report emergencies to the appropriate authorities. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
entertainment.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. By reintroducing daily non-stop frequency on both routes, ValueJet provides critical operational flexibility for holiday travelers. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. Simultaneously, the Asaba–Abuja route delivers a direct, hassle-free link between the nation’s capital and Asaba, eliminating lengthy road journeys and complex connection itineraries. The resumption complements ValueJet’s rapidly expanding domestic and regional network. Domestically, the airline provides essential air links to key destinations including Port Harcourt, Jos, Owerri, Calabar, Benin, and GWI-Iperu. Beyond Nigeria’s borders, ValueJet continues to extend its reach beyond established destinations like Accra, Banjul, Cotonou, and Malabo with upcoming regional route expansions to Libreville, Monrovia, and Abidjan. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. SHOW AND AVAILABILITY Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: Empowers Over 10,000 Women to Build Wealth and Financial Independence
entertainment.description: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair , a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership. Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele , Omoni Oboli , BamBam , Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo , for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. Olufemi Shobanjo of NGX Regulation Limited shared insights into capital market participation, while actress BamBam, marketing strategist and Woof Studios founder Adetutu Laditan, and Mercy Agbeti, popularly known as Christian Money Woman, contributed to conversations about building value, navigating opportunities and growing with purpose. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026

The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. sports.title: Fran Gonzalez explains his decision to leave Real Madrid – “You have other dreams”
sports.description: Fran Gonzalez explains his decision to leave Real Madrid – “You have other dreams” Fran Gonzalez was one of the less talked-about exits for Real Madrid in a summer that was saw a lot of action. The young goalkeeper, after multiple years with the club’s academy, left Real Madrid to join Sevilla on a deal worth €3 million . Although Gonzalez has yet to make a breakthrough at Sevilla, he has recently explained his decision to leave Real Madrid in the summer in great detail. Gonzalez on leaving Real Madrid Fran Gonzalez only ever featured in one game for Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) When asked about his decision to leave the Spanish capital, Gonzalez pointed some key reasons including the desire to make it elsewhere. “I had closed a chapter there in Madrid, with Castilla, and I believed the best thing for me was to take that leap, wherever it might be,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). “Obviously, it’s normal for young goalkeepers not to play right away, no matter where they go, because I come from the Primera RFEF, a competition that has improved a lot in recent years, but it’s a big step. I feel very prepared to make that leap,” he added. Gonzalez explained he had felt his time at Real Madrid academy had come to an end and it was time for a new challenge elsewhere. “I felt that I had finished a stage, and Sevilla is one of the great clubs in Spain, a truly historic club, very good in every sense, and a real opportunity for me to compete and play in the coming years, ” he said. Gonzalez on joining Sevilla Fran Gonzalez spent multiple years at La Fabrica . (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Gonzalez admitted it was quite painful to leave Valdebebas, as he hailed Real Madrid as the best club in the world. However, the goalkeeper admitted it was his desire to join Sevilla and that he was drawn to the opportunity. “It’s not easy to leave what is probably the best club in the world, but well, many times you have other dreams and my dream was to come to Sevilla, from the first moment I was very clear about it. “I didn’t even have to think about it, it’s a place to continue growing and to be able to stay for a long time ,” he concluded. Gonzalez’s spell at Sevilla, though, has started off slowly, with his only appearance this season coming in Copa Del Rey. He is still comfortably behind Odysseas Vlachodimos in the pecking order. However, the young Spaniard is confident he can soon fight for a place in the first-team and is ready to exercise patience.

sports.description: GLOCESTER – The note had been attached to her mirror since the end of a disappointing junior season, serving as a subtle reminder to what her big goal was for her senior season. Perhaps the message wasn’t so subtle. Alyssa Parenteau wanted to win the 2026 RIIL Girls Cross Country State Championship and on Saturday, did just that. In a sport that comes a little more difficult to the All-State track star, Parenteau managed to grind through the season and grinder harder through the wet and muddy course at Ponaganset High School. She emptied the tank and nearly ran out of gas at the end, but crossed in a time of 18:16.33, holding off South Kingstown freshman Emma Morrissey by 1.12 seconds. “This honestly feels surreal,” said Parenteau after becoming La Salle’s first champion since Kaylie Armitage in 2019. “I’ve done it in track, but the cross country title tops it so much. Girls cross country is so much harder for me. “… I have to put in double the work mentally and physically, so the fact I was able to come out here today and do this was surreal for me.” While Parenteau was a first-time winner, the team champions were hardly new to the top of the podium. Cumberland gave other teams a glimmer of hope after punting on the Class Championships, but left little doubt about the condition of their dynasty. The Clippers had two runners in the top six, three in the top eight and five in the top 11 to score 40 points, 31 ahead of runner-up La Salle, winning their fourth straight team crowd. “It’s such a crazy thing that we have a team that’s capable of doing this four years in a row,” said junior Cecelia Ludwig after Cumberland became the first public school to win four straight since North Kingstown won five from 2000-2004. “Coming back ever single year to have the confidence that we can do stuff like this, it’s incredible to have that opportunity.” Hampered by injuries as a sophomore, Parenteau had a championship opportunity last fall following her first Class A Championship. It wasn’t meant to be, as she finished seventh at the state meet, leading her to write a note about her big goal for 2026 and stick it on a mirror so she could see it every day. Confidence was key to Parenteau’s success this fall. It built throughout the season and shined in her second straight Class A title.
